label: Human Factors
text_excerpt: I was practicing slip to landing. Winds were variable and I was coming in high originally. By the time I came into ground-effect I was lower and slower than intended. Due to this I landed slightly short of the displaced runway threshold line. I then exited runway as soon as able and taxied to parking.

label: Aircraft
text_excerpt: Last reported wind light and variable. The wind was calm. Touchdown was normal. Nosewheel was lowered to the runway. Aircraft rapidly veered off centerline to the left. Full right rudder had no effect. Aircraft departed runway and came to rest near the parallel taxiway. My passenger and I were the only occupants. We were not injured. There was no property damage. There were no witnesses. The aircraft sustained some damage. I have owned and operated this airplane since it was new 34 years ago. This was the first and only incident. The mechanical malfunction has not been determined.

No altitude was lost; and the PLI may have momentarily flashed. 'Bank Angle' aural warning sounded during the event and recovery.

label: Weather
text_excerpt: Lightning strike during climb out on ZZZ from runway XXR at 6200 feet. We were in a right turn heading 040 per ATC. I was hand flying and looking at my instruments when I noticed some Saint Elmo's fire on my windshield; then saw the lightning bolt in front of me. It was startlingly bright; and we all saw it and felt it. Continued climb and reported incident to ATC. Once out of weather and 10 000 feet; assessed aircraft. All cockpit instrument; readings; gages; indications; EICAS; and status messages were normal but flight attendants were reporting on and off electrical burning smell in front of aircraft. Had FO fly aircraft and handle radio to set up SAT COM call with dispatch & maintenance.

text_excerpt: Apparently several legs before my flight; a belt loader had hit the aircraft just below the aft cargo door. I was waiting for the aircraft; so I was quickly outside for the walkaround once it arrived. They were still unloading bags during my walkaround; so I guess that loader blocked my view of the damage. It didn't cause anything irregular in flight and was notified until a week and a half later that the damage had been there. If whoever initially impacted the aircraft had alerted the crew; or perhaps as the ground crew pulled up; they probably had an unobstructed view of the damage.
